top_posts.title: The Secrets of the 'delete' Operator in JavaScript
top_posts.summary: The delete operator in JavaScript is used to remove a property reference from an object. It returns true on successful deletion and false on failure. It only works on the object's own properties and not on prototype chain properties. Non-existent properties will return true but have no effect. Non-configurable, and properties declared with var, let, or const cannot be deleted. For arrays, non-configurable properties like length cannot be deleted and attempting to do so in strict mode throws a TypeError.

Practical examples for each property demonstrate how to enhance user experience on web pages.
